title: C2 - shuffling the options must not move the distribution
note: The same question with its criteria map written in three different key orders. Nothing about the judgment changed, so nothing about the distribution should. If order matters anywhere it will show on the ambiguous state, where probability is genuinely split and a tie-break has something to bite on. Result: the two unambiguous states are perfectly order-invariant (TV 0.000). The ambiguous one is not. Across three orderings the winning option held at 'returns', but its probability moved 0.62 -> 0.48 -> 0.58 and confidence moved 0.43 -> 0.22 -> 0.37, a TV distance of 0.14. The selected answer is stable; the number a confidence gate reads is not. Code that routes on a threshold near 0.3 would send the same ticket down different paths depending only on the order the criteria dict was written in.
